messages:
maya: alert from infra-bot — gpu-pool headroom in eu-west-1 is oscillating, admission-control toggled twice in the last 10m. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/pools/eu-west-1
infra-bot: [ALERT] gpu_pool_headroom_pct(eu-west-1) dropped below 12% -> ADMISSION_CONTROL=ENABLED at 2026-05-12T15:22:57Z
ashwin: seeing same on metrics. queue_len spiked to ~420 for hosted-small pool, 95th latency also increased briefly.
leo: can you paste the prometheus query you used?
maya: sure — used: `sum(gpu_pool_headroom_percent{region="eu-west-1"}) by (pool)`, and `max_over_time(admission_control_state[10m])` to confirm flapping.
ashwin: also ran `rate(admission_control_drops_total[5m])` — showed a short burst of drops ~15/s for ~2m.
ops-sre: network flapping between rack-3 and storage-tier-1 earlier; link-spike at 15:20 may have coincided. NOC ticket 7892.
leo: interesting — headroom oscillation could be autoscaler reacting to transient load + small scale step size. our autoscaler cooldown is 60s now.
maya: current mitigations I pushed: 1) disabled aggressive scale-down for hosted-small for 10m, 2) increased alert smoothing window from 2m -> 6m, 3) created short-term reservation: `infra-cli reserve-pool --region eu-west-1 --pool hosted-small --gpus 6 --reason "temp headroom bump"`
marie: thanks. are we going to adjust admission-control thresholds or keep as is?
ashwin: recommend keep thresholds but increase lower-bound headroom threshold to 8% instead of 5% while we investigate autoscaler behavior. that reduces flap-triggering.
ops-sre: applied threshold change on staging, will roll to prod if no regressions.
leo: also filed COGS note — small bursts cost us due to cold start of extra nodes. ticket INFRA-2141.
maya: action items: (1) follow NOC ticket 7892 for network root cause, (2) monitor headroom and admission drops for next 2 hours, (3) if spike again, call for immediate capacity bump in eu-west-1.
marie: ack :thumbsup:
infra-bot: [INFO] Reservation created: id=resv-5312, gpus=6, expires=2026-05-12T17:22:57Z
leo: will also look at autoscaler configs — maybe increase scale step to avoid oscillation on short-lived spikes.
